text: Therefore, I would like to ask the Senior Minister of State what specific measures can be taken to curb platform operators from raising prices and passing on the increased cost to consumers?

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Furthermore, platform operators may also reduce benefits for platform workers in order to lower their operating cost.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: If this happens, platform workers will be affected and will not be able to enjoy the protection they deserve.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: If so, can the new platform work associations also negotiate with private hire car rental companies, which are prevalent and currently not regulated by the Land Transport Authority (LTA)?

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: While private hire car and taxi driving is limited to Singaporeans, many delivery workers are permanent residents (PRs).

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Will the platform work associations represent these PRs?

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Thirdly, section 39(4) states that at least two-thirds of the officers of every registered platform work association must be active platform service providers.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Should this proportion not be higher, given that the associations are meant for platform workers?

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: In addition, should officers of these platform work associations be required to work a minimum number of hours each month to better stay connected and relevant to the platform workers?

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: However, for platform drivers, injuries from road accidents could be covered under a car insurance policy if the driver is not at fault.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: How would MOM advise platform drivers on whether to claim through their car insurance or the work injury compensation insurance for road accidents?

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: This is about recognising the hard work and contributions of platform workers and giving them the protection and respect they deserve.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Our platform workers perform important services utilised by many Singaporeans and residents.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: They should be accorded similar protections and benefits as employees in similar wage bands.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: The proposals in the Bill are greatly welcomed since they will help boost their retirement and housing adequacies and get the necessary compensation and representation.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I am heartened that many of the suggestions, feedback and appeals by my Parliamentary colleagues and me to improve the welfare of platform workers over the past few years have been incorporated into this Bill.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: My residents in Fernvale will certainly be delighted to know that this law will be passed in Parliament.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Three years should be enough for all to adapt and allow platform workers to start accumulating more CPF savings earlier.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: In addition, among platform workers born before 1995, a significant proportion would be beneficiaries of the Workfare Income Supplement (WIS) scheme.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Due to their age, their income, compared to fellow workers, may not be as high.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Hence, the Government can consider letting them join the CPF scheme so that they can benefit and be given the WIS as additional income.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: On behalf of platform workers, I would like to thank the government.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: However, there seems to be no such regulations for platform workers.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: There is a risk of platform workers being overworked and not being adequately paid for the additional hours or compensated for higher risks of working while fatigued.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Will the Ministry consider looking into this and implementing measures to ensure that platform workers are adequately protected?

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: At the Sitting in July 2021, I had asked MOM to consider mandatory breaks for drivers of private hire cars to mitigate health and safety concerns relating to driver fatigue from continuous driving.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: As drivers are paid for the number of trips they make, I am also deeply concerned about the dangers of overwork for such platform workers.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I hope the Ministry will consider looking into the use of technology to support the drivers to take a short break if the need arises, if they are tired and reduce the safety risks to themselves and others, including their families.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I would also like to take this opportunity to highlight an issue in our current driving framework.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: For taxi services, the taxi driver must be aged 30 and above and be a Singapore Citizen.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: However, for GrabHitch driver-partner services, PRs and those aged below 30 are allowed to provide driving services.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: On the surface, GrabHitch is a social car-pooling service which allows all drivers to give a lift to riders heading the same way.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: In practice, this may be a loophole which enables foreigners and younger, less experienced drivers to provide driver services.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: How will the authorities check and ensure that the drivers are genuine social drivers?

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Rooting out unqualified persons would help protect the livelihoods of our genuine platform workers.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Last but not least, there have been cases of foreigners coming to Singapore to do delivery work.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: How would the Ministry tighten the regulations and increase enforcement to ensure that these illegal workers do not encroach upon the livelihoods of our local platform workers, depress their wages and, if accidents were to happen to them, and others.

speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
text: They are sons and daughters, fathers and mothers, and even grandparents.

speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
text: In my conversations with them, I have learned about their tireless efforts and the sacrifices they make.

speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
text: Many endure long hours on the road, at times, 12, 15, or even 18 hours a day, driven by a profound commitment to provide for their families and secure a better future for their children.

speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
text: One rider proudly shared with me that his two children are students in schools running the Integrated Programme, with one in junior college and the other in secondary school, both working hard to succeed.

speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
text: These children are not only their parents' motivating force and hope, but they are also the next generation of Singapore.

speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
text: It is thus our collective responsibility to safeguard the wellbeing of these hardworking individuals who are devoted to their families and play a pivotal role in building our nation.

speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
text: One of the most pressing concerns we must address is the safety of our delivery riders.

speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
text: The extended hours they work are not just gruelling, they pose significant risks on the road.

speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
text: Fatigue from long hours is a serious safety hazard that increases the likelihood of accidents.

speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
text: To mitigate this, it is essential for the Government and platform operators to work together to enhance safety guidelines.

speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
text: In many industries, shift workers are provided with mandatory breaks, shift limits and other safety protocols.

speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
text: Implementing similar safeguards for delivery riders could significantly reduce the dangers they face on the road and ensure their safety as they carry out their work.

speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
text: Balancing safety with economic needs is also critical.

speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
text: I understand that some riders may be concerned about limits on their working hours due to the urgency of providing for their families and the uncertainty of securing jobs.

speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
text: Platform work does not always guarantee a consistent income as earnings depend on the availability of jobs in specific locations and time slots.

speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
text: Those who do not earn enough during their shift may feel compelled to extend their working hours to make up the gaps in income.

speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
text: However, those extra hours could just lead to a devastating loss of a breadwinner due to a preventable accident.

speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
text: The number of consecutive hours riders are allowed to work and how incentives are given are part of these arrangements.

speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
text: It is important that the Government and the industry continue to work closely to clarify how these provisions will be implemented, enforce them rigorously and review them regularly to safeguard our workers on the road.

speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
text: From the delivery workers I have spoken with, there is genuine appreciation for this provision.

speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
text: It offers a structured approach to savings, provide financial security for those with young families and those who may not have the means or knowledge to save adequately on their own.

speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
text: Many riders who are also breadwinners often prioritise and are very willing to spend on their family's present needs, leaving little for their own retirement.

speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
text: The Platform Workers Bill stands out not only for its comprehensive safety and financial provisions but also for the collaborative process behind its creation.

speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
text: While other countries have taken steps to address platform worker rights, Singapore's Platform Workers Bill excels in its comprehensive approach to challenges such as retirement adequacy, work safety and insurance, and collective representation.

speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
text: This achievement is rooted in Singapore's distinctive approach to tripartism, which brings together the voices of workers, employers and the Government to shape policies.

speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
text: Thanks to the tireless efforts of our tripartite partners: MOM, the National Trades Union Congress (NTUC) and the Singapore National Employers Federation (SNEF), we are able to introduce a Bill that safeguards platform workers in a balanced and efficient manner.

speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
text: In contrast, we can observe the challenges of a different approach in California.

speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
text: In 2020, the introduction of Assembly Bill 5, also known as AB5, which aimed to reclassify platform workers as employees, was swiftly challenged by platform companies through Proposition 22, a measure that exempted platform operators from AB5's requirements.

speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
text: This led to a prolonged legal battle that lasted years and concluded in July 2024 with Proposition 22 being held in favour of platform operators.

speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
text: The process not only incurred significant legal costs for both employers and unions, but also delayed the much-needed protections for workers.

speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
text: Singapore's collaborative tripartite model, on the other hand, enables a smoother roll-out of protections, avoiding prolonged conflicts and ensuring that all stakeholders are engaged from the start.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: A couple of years ago, I had a meeting at a platform operator’s headquarters office in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: And the person I was meeting suggested to let us meet at the staff cafeteria.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: So, I went to the staff cafeteria, and I remembered being blown away.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: It was a very nice cafeteria, offering a full range of wholesome meals to staff; there was also an espresso machine and freshly brewed coffee and even beer, for after office hours, I presume.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: And it was lunch time when I visited, so the whole cafeteria was lively, teeming with employees, lots of laughter and conversations and energy, and everyone was just enjoying themselves and having a good time in this staff cafeteria.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: I recall looking at this and thinking about the delivery riders who were waiting for orders at the fast-food outlet at the CC in my constituency.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: And I recalled thinking, both groups of workers are working for the same platform company, contributing to the platform company, so why is the difference in perks, benefits and experience so large?

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: If passed, it will be a great leap forward for the rights and protection of platform workers in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: Platform workers deserve rights and protection under our laws.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: And I am glad that there is broad political consensus on this fundamental point – indeed, both the Workers' Party (WP) and Progress Singapore Party (PSP) support the Bill and agree with the Government on this fundamental point.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: The Platform Workers Bill has been described as a "landmark" Bill.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: But the Bill is landmark not only for what it will achieve – for the rights and protection of platform workers, if passed.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: It is also landmark for how we are able to achieve it in the first place, make the Bill possible in the first place, because of who we are, and how we work.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: It is landmark for how we are able to achieve the Bill in the first place because of who we are and how we work.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: This landmark Bill is only possible because of our unique tripartism in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: There are so many innovative and groundbreaking features in this wide-ranging piece of legislation.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: Take for example, the Work Injury Compensation framework for platform workers.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: Senior Minister of State Koh circulated this nifty A3-sized brochure in his opening speech yesterday to summarise the framework, but let us think about it.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: The principles and the basic mechanism of Work Injury Compensation for platform workers that this brochure so neatly summarises are thoughtful, measured, balanced, very carefully crafted.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: It must have taken months and months of hard work, by tripartite partners, by a competent Government, working closely with an NTUC who is all about creating better lives for workers, with platform workers themselves, and with platform operators, insurers and other business stakeholders.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: These Fixed Expense Deduction Amount factors and the whole concept of Fixed Expense Deduction Amount itself, they are another major innovation.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: But they did not drop from the sky.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: Rather, they are borne of what must, again, have been months and months of hard work, of respectful, collaborative consultations between Government, NTUC, platform workers, and platform operators.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: I can imagine putting five platform workers, operator representatives, union leaders and Government representatives in the same room and asking them to try to agree on this Fixed Expense Deduction Amount values.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: And between the five of them, there would probably be six different views, and ask them to come back the next day, there may yet be another three or four different views.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: But with our unique model of tripartism, we got it done.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: And so, our unique model of tripartism in Singapore made this landmark Bill possible.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: And I say, we should celebrate and applaud this achievement by our unique tripartism in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: And yes, there will be challenges and key issues to implementing the Bill, as has been discussed extensively in this debate.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: There will certainly be challenges, but I am confident that if we continue to rely on our unique tripartism and work through our unique tripartism, we can – and we will – overcome all these challenges.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: Platform workers, through platform work associations, and platform operators will have full flexibility to determine the scope of this collective bargaining.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: It is my hope that pay, specifically fair pay, will be a key issue that our tripartite partners will pick up and address in the collective bargaining going forward.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: Compared to the comments that have been offered by a major operator recently that its base fare is, I quote, "benchmarked to the F&B sector" and "something like $1,400", I think we are quite some way off the mark today.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: The key is also to make these earnings more stable, more consistent week to week, month on month, around the agreed average, so as to reduce the precarity of pay for platform work.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: It will not be easy to achieve and we will not be able to wait for another Institute of Policy Studies survey or the annual survey by MOM to tell us how we are doing on fair pay for our platform workers.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: To achieve this, we really need a monitoring and calibration logic cycle that is as dynamic as the algorithms that are assigning gigs, churning out jobs, putting out fares and incentives.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: Indeed, we will probably need to bake the whole logic of fair pay into the operating algorithms of platform operators for this to really work.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: The task will be fraught with complexities: there are the vagaries of supply and demand in the gig economy; there are variances in the base fare and incentive structures across time and across operators; there are various types of platform work to begin with and there are other complexities to work through.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: But a basic principle that we can all agree on, around what constitutes fair pay for platform work, will become a north star that can guide and anchor everyone, all stakeholders, as we work through these complexities.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: So, we should do it, because it is right for our platform workers.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: And we can do it, I believe, because we have our unique model of tripartism in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: Let us not stop at pay but let us also champion and advance pay progression for platform work.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: It is often said that platform work provides "almost zero" prospects of career advancement and pay progression.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: I say, let us harness the collective bargaining structure for platform work that this Bill will enable to break these boundaries, to break that whole mental model.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: And let us contemplate and work towards, through collective bargaining, a future where we can provide some skills ladder, job ladder and pay ladder for various types of platform work.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: It will be challenging and there is no precedent around the world.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: But if there is anywhere in the world that can take a shot at this and do this, it is in Singapore, with our unique model of tripartism.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: And if we can get it done, it will be truly innovative and groundbreaking for platform workers and the platform work economy in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: (In Mandarin):   The Platform Workers Bill aims to provide platform workers with appropriate rights and protections under our laws.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: Platform workers deserve to have rights and protections.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: However, this Platform Workers Bill did not come about by chance, but rather as a result of our unique Tripartite model, which has made this Platform Workers Bill possible.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: Looking to the future, we must also rely on our unique Tripartite model to continue to advocate for the rights and protections of platform workers and allow the legal effects of this Bill be maximised in practice.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: By doing this, the income, welfare and lives of platform workers will improve continuously. : Sir, to conclude, ultimately, this Bill is not only pro-worker but also, in my mind, pro-business and pro-consumer.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: It is about the ethos of business that we want in Singapore – businesses that do well by doing good and doing right.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: It is also about the Singaporean consumer supporting fair and sustainable trade practices.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: It is about an ever fairer economy and an ever fairer and more just society in Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: In my opening speech yesterday, I went into some length to explain the construct of the Bill and some of the implementation details for CPF contribution, work injury compensation and representation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Members will get a sense of how complex it is to implement the recommendations put forth by the Advisory Committee for Platform Workers – and Mr Xie Yao Quan's speech just before mine, gave a very good glimpse into the complexities of the negotiations and, sometimes, all the to-ing the fro-ing, all the arguments that can take place.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: But eventually, we landed on a good set of recommendations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Before I address the specific questions raised by Members, I thought it is useful for me to help Members of this House understand how we are able to put forth this landmark legislation to help a group of workers who are precarious, when many other countries are still grappling to solve their problems.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: The platform sector is a very heterogeneous one that is rapidly evolving and, sometimes, new ones will come onto the scene as well.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: A key characteristic is the very dynamic way in which supply and demand of jobs and labour are very quickly matched, and dynamic pricing also serves to incentivise service users and workers to facilitate a match.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Platform operators, workers and users interact with one another dynamically as demand/supply and prices respond and change rapidly in real time.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This allows flexibility and is a feature platform workers desire but it also imposes management control on these workers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Multi-homing on various platforms further adds to the complexity.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: For these reasons, many countries are grappling with the difficulties of putting a legislative frame around a constantly evolving entity.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: How did we manage to put forth this Platform Workers Bill today, that both the governing and opposition Members have given their unanimous support to, in such a short time, over a mere two to three years since we started this stream of work?

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: The International Labour Organization (ILO) is also interested to understand how we did it.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: I will share three key ingredients that made this possible.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: It is a relationship that is forged through the crucible of time, with which we had weathered various crises together over the decades.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: It allows us to adopt a collaborative approach to seek win-win solutions and enables us to nimby adapt and adjust to the fast-evolving nature of the platform landscape.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This is something that is unique and special here in Singapore that is not necessarily the case in many other countries.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: The Director-General of ILO Mr Gilbert Houngbo has shared his admiration for the unique tripartism we have here in Singapore when I met him in Geneva and he is keen to learn more about how our tripartism actually works.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: But what is so unique about our tripartism?

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We must understand that there is a natural tension between the interests of businesses and workers which stems from the competing goals of maximising profits on the one side, and securing fair treatment and compensation on the other.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: It is quite easy for a government to be pro-worker.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: It is also quite easy for a government to be pro-business.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: But it is very difficult for a government to be both pro-worker and pro-business at the same time.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Close relationships between unions and political parties are perfectly normal in all functioning democracies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This usually takes the form of the union either forming a party on its own or funding and supporting one party.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: A cornerstone of our strong tripartite relationship is the symbiotic relationship between PAP and NTUC as well as our respect for the employers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Tripartism undergirds the industrial harmony and economic success of Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Other countries try to emulate us, but they cannot because, unlike us, they do not have the symbiotic relationship between unions and the governing party, and so they do not have the tripartism that we have.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: What is dangerously clear to us is that the WP will seek to dismantle this.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: When the WP attacks the symbiotic relationship between the PAP and NTUC and Mr Gerald Giam said, and I quote, "I believe that unions must be independent and non-partisan", he is, in fact, saying that the WP will not align itself with any union or form any relationship with any union.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: The WP will kill tripartism, and in its place will be a more adversarial form of relationship and system that we see happening elsewhere.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: David Marshall was the founding Chairman of the WP.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: When David Marshall mooted the idea of forming a "political party whose membership is exclusively confined to members of trade unions" and started the WP in 1957, the founding executive committee members of the party comprised 20 trade unionists and 10 non-unionists.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Mr Gerald Giam and the WP are completely ignorant about how the WP started as a party of unionists.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: And some of this information was obtained from their own website.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Clearly, the WP is no longer a pro-worker party.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Unions have long been a part of WP's history.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Somehow, along the way, they lost the trust in their relationship with the unions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: So, now, Mr Gerald Giam says, like a bit of a toxic ex-boyfriend, because I cannot have a relationship with unions, no one else should have as well; there should be no love between any other political party and the unions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: So, I thank the members of PWAC for their efforts that made this possible.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: The second ingredient is a strong and dedicated team of civil servants at MOM.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Beyond the recommendations of PWAC, Members can appreciate the very complex implementation mechanisms and operational processes that insurers, platform operators, CPF Board and MOM will need to put in place to ensure seamless and smooth execution for CPF collection, an effective work injury compensation claims regime and a workable representation framework.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: My MOM colleagues have worked closely with the platform operators, our tripartite partners NTUC and SNEF as well as various agencies, taking their feedback and working through various policy and operational constructs to address the complex nature of work in this sector.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Mr Xie Yao Quan's speech just now characterised some of these challenges in coming up with very detailed implementation details.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Sometimes, I look at my officers and I think, the kind of mental gymnastics that they do to come up with all these implementation details, deserves an Olympic medal.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: I want to put on record my thanks to all of them for their dedication and commitment to strengthening the support and protections for our platform workers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Various surveys have shown that Singaporeans are prepared to pay a little bit more to give these platform workers better protection.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: The percentages may vary across different surveys taken at different time points, but that is not the main thing.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Recognising that "every worker matters" means that platform workers also deserve to be treated fairly and equitably.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We will have to make trade-offs and accept that not all the issues and gaps in the platform space can be fully addressed through this legislation alone.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: But the status quo of leaving this group of workers – these platform workers, who are vulnerable – would not be the right thing to do.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: In legislating, we seek to preserve the key characteristics of the platform economy to ensure it can still function effectively, even as we seek to reduce the precarity of platform workers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: All stakeholders, including consumers, will need to play a part.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Some Members have expressed concerns that the introduction of the Bill will raise prices.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: On the other hand, there have also been calls to do more for platform workers to provide even more protections for them.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: With this principle in mind, I will now address the queries and concerns raised by broad themes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Some of the questions raised by Members have already been addressed in my speech yesterday, so I will not cover them here again.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: I will start by addressing questions related to the first set of amendments on the definition of terms and scope of entities and workers covered under the Bill.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Many Members have suggested expanding the scope of the Bill to cover other platform services beyond that of the ride-hail and delivery services.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: As I have earlier explained, the Bill will account for the vast majority of platform workers doing work that is precarious.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: That said, I would like to assure Members we will certainly review the scope of the Act in the future, as the platform landscape continues to evolve.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Mr Patrick Tay had a query on the meaning of "agreement" in clause 5(1)(a) of the Bill.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Clause 5(1) sets out the conditions that must be met for the purposes of determining if an individual is a platform worker.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: The "agreement" in clause 5(1) will become a "platform work agreement" only when an individual satisfies all conditions to be a platform worker.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Mr Tay also sought clarification on the meaning of "special expenses" in the definition of "earnings" in the Bill. "Special expenses" include payments meant to reimburse the expenses of platform workers when providing the platform service.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: An example would be the reimbursement of costs that platform workers may incur for cleaning services if a customer makes a mess in the vehicle.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Such expenses will not attract CPF contributions as they are not meant to add to the platform worker's earnings.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Mr Neil Parekh had a query on how existing contracts will be affected and how conflicts between the Bill and platform work agreements will be resolved.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This means that even if existing agreements are not revised or the platform operator does not enter into any new agreement with the platform worker, the Act will supersede any existing platform work agreement.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Therefore, it is in the interest of platform operators to go through existing agreements or enter into new agreements with their platform workers to reflect the new obligations under the Act.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Mr Pritam Singh and Ms Yeo Wan Ling have expressed concerns about the impact of increased CPF contributions on platform workers' take-home pay.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Platform workers can use their Ordinary Account contributions in lieu of cash to pay for their housing loans.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: As mentioned in my speech yesterday, we have enhanced the PCTS to offset 100% and 75% of the year-on-year increase in the first and second year respectively.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Mr Pritam Singh's remark that the 100% PCTS offset applies to the lowest increase is not true as the increase in each year is up to 2.5% points.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Ms Yeo Wan Ling asked whether the PCTS can be extended to all platform workers who earn more than $2,500, for up to the first $2,500 of their earnings.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: The PCTS is targeted at lower-income platform workers to provide them with monthly support in the transition period when they see a decrease in their take-home pay as they would have less disposable income for their daily expenses.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Mr Sharael Taha asked if part-time platform workers would be covered by the CPF provisions and be eligible for the PCTS and Workfare Income Supplement.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: The CPF provisions do apply to part-time platform workers, and neither PCTS nor Workfare eligibility is dependent on whether the worker is working part-time or full-time as a platform worker.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This is in line with the flexible nature of platform work because the worker can choose the number of hours he or she wants to work.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Mr Gan Thiam Poh asked if we would consider reducing the phase-in of CPF contribution rates from five years to three years and Mr Louis Chua asked to introduce the full increase for platform operators immediately.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Mr Gan, Mr Pritam Singh and Assoc Prof Jamus Lim also suggested making the CPF scheme compulsory for older cohorts of platform workers or making older cohorts opt out of CPF contributions rather than opt in.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Underlying their suggestions is the sentiment that CPF contributions are very important for all platform workers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: But there are pertinent considerations behind the proposed construct that we have put forth.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: The five-year phase-in period was a careful decision we made, considering the take-home pay impact on platform workers, the cost impact on platform operators and the possible costs that could be passed on to consumers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: These are also concerns raised by various Members in their speeches.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: A five-year phase-in period will allow any impact to the various stakeholders to be moderated and allows time for the market to adjust to a new equilibrium.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: For platform workers who wish to achieve higher CPF contributions earlier than 2029, they can make voluntary CPF contributions to all three accounts in their CPF between 2025 and 2028, and benefit from tax relief for these additional voluntary contributions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: The decision to allow older platform workers to choose whether to participate in the increased CPF contributions by opting in recognises that they may already have existing plans to finance their housing and retirement needs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Some may have already finished paying their home loans.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Older platform workers in many of our engagement sessions expressed preference for the choice to opt in.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We respect these preferences that older platform workers have expressed to us.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This is why we have allowed older cohorts to opt in, rather than including all by default and requiring them to opt out.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: The opt-in arrangement allows platform workers to carefully consider their needs and plans before consciously choosing to increase their CPF contributions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: If it is on an opt-out basis, there may be some who might only realise later that their CPF contributions increased and will want to withdraw.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This would be administratively onerous on both the platform workers and platform operators.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Nonetheless, I do encourage older platform workers to make a conscious decision and take the active step to choose increased CPF contributions from the start, especially if they are servicing a housing loan or want to build up their savings for retirement.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Furthermore, a study by the Institute of Policy Studies found that younger platform workers expressed stronger preference for additional CPF contributions to help meet their housing needs as they were more likely to have housing obligations or plans to buy a house.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Younger cohorts would also benefit more from the compounding of interest, given the longer runway for accumulation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Members would appreciate that platform work is a very heterogeneous space.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Different individuals participate in platform work for various reasons and to various extents.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Some do it full-time as their main source of income, others do it part-time to supplement their other sources of income.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Yet others do it ad hoc to just get some pocket money.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Ms Mariam Jaafar and Assoc Prof Jamus Lim asked about how we plan to encourage platform workers to opt in or to help strengthen their financial literacy.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: The Government is working with partners, including NTUC and Institute for Financial Literacy (IFL) to ensure that platform workers are aware of the benefits of opting in to the increased CPF contributions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: IFL will also offer holistic financial literacy guidance for platform workers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman, Mr Ong Hua Han, Mr Pritam Singh and Assoc Prof Jamus Lim spoke about platform workers potentially facing discrimination because of their CPF contributions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: There was a suggestion to police or audit the platform operators' algorithm to ensure that it does not result in discrimination against platform workers who opt in for CPF.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: First, an algorithm is quite dynamic, responding to real-time changes in demand and supply for platform services.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Any audit will be reactive and of limited utility.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: The moment you get the algorithm and audit it, something has changed in the next one hour and you will always be chasing the tail.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: If we force platform operators to reveal such knowledge, this may drive them away and bring about a loss of platform worker jobs, which is not our desired outcome for these workers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Platform work associations will have the legal mandate to represent the interest of the platform workers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: If there are instances of possible discriminatory practices by any platform operator, the platform work association can take this up with the relevant operators and, where necessary, inform MOM.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This provides a channel for the platform workers, through the platform work associations, to communicate and negotiate with the platform operators.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Similar to the trade union space, this can be done in a way that seeks to achieve win-win outcomes and preserves the harmonious relationship between the platform workers and platform operators in this fast evolving industry.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: In addition, because of the cohort-based approach, an increasing proportion of platform workers will be covered by mandatory CPF contributions over time, as the years go by.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Over time, all the younger workers who take on platform work will have mandatory CPF contributions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Therefore, it is in the interest of platform operators to treat all platform workers fairly, regardless of whether they opt-in or are in the mandatory cohort.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: It is therefore also in the interest of platform operators to treat all workers fairly from the perspective of worker retention.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Mr Ang Wei Neng asked about the CPF contribution rates for platform workers aged above 55.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: As mentioned, the contribution rates set out in the schedule of the Bill are subject to the CPF contribution rate increases for employees in the same age group.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Mr Sharael Taha asked how expenses will be factored in for platform workers who use multiple modes of transport.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: The Fixed Expense Deduction Amount to be applied will be based on the mode of transport for the specific job in question.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Next, I will cover the clarifications regarding the third set of amendments to ensure financial protection of platform workers if they get injured at work and to strengthen stakeholders’ responsibilities to prevent injuries.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Mr Pritam Singh asked about the cost impact of work injury compensation insurance premiums on platform operators.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Mr Desmond Choo, Mr Mark Lee and Ms Yeo Wan Ling sought clarifications on the work injury compensation process for cases where multiple platform operators are involved.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: There was also a suggestion for a centralised insurance system to minimise disputes over which platform operator is liable for the claim.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: While I agree with the need for fair and expeditious compensation, a monopolistic approach is not the best way to provide for platform workers’ insurance needs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: In comparison, allowing platform operators to purchase work injury compensation insurance in an open and competitive market facilitates sustainable premiums.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: The open market allows platform operators to negotiate insurance rates with insurers of their choice and a competitive market facilitates sustainable premiums based on claims history.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: As with employers, platform operators’ insurance premiums will account for the risks in the sectors they operate in, which Ms Mariam Jaafar asked about.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This will be based on indicators such as payroll size and number of workers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We welcome other players to join the market as well.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Nevertheless, we agree with Members that it is important for platform workers to receive compensation in a timely manner, so they can recuperate from a work injury with peace of mind.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: An injured platform worker only needs to inform the platform operator he is working for of the incident and his injury details.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: The platform operator will file a work injury report to MOM and the platform operator’s insurer will be notified to process the work injury compensation claim.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: The platform worker will be notified of the work injury compensation claim case reference number and the insurer processing the claim.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: As with the employee regime, insurers and platform operators will be required to follow operational timelines for the processing of claims expeditiously, and the same dispute resolution mechanisms apply.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Ms Jean See asked about plans to augment the Bill to protect platform workers against the unintended consequences of safety regulations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Mr Gan Thiam Poh suggested regulating the working hours of platform workers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Mr Melvin Yong suggested for platform workers to have training for road safety and safe load management and to codify incentive structures.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: From our engagements, platform workers value the flexibility to determine how long and when to work, which helps them accommodate personal commitments.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: The proposed Bill should not alter the flexible nature of platform work that is a key feature of platform work that both the workers and the platform operators desire.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Nonetheless, we agree this should not be at the cost to personal safety and health of platform workers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Hence, amendments to the WSH Act will empower platform workers to prioritise safety and prevent platform operators from penalising them for doing so.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Developed with tripartite partners, platform operators and platform workers, the Approved Code of Practice will codify how platform operators and platform workers can collectively address safety concerns in platform work, including fatigue management and support platform workers’ access to safety training.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: It includes what Mr Leong Mun Wai suggested – that platform operators should not penalise platform workers who were unable to complete the job for valid reasons.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: With these in place, we should allow the industry to take ownership and work on its safety practices.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Intervening to micromanage the incentive structures and algorithms of platform operators or the working hours of platform workers risks jeopardising the flexibility and sustainability of platform work.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Next, I will address questions on the fourth set of amendments on the legal framework for representation of platform workers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: I will also speak on how some of the suggestions raised by members are more suited to be taken up by platform work associations in negotiations with platform operators.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Mr Patrick Tay asked how MOM would determine when platform workers have undertaken industrial action.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Industrial action refers to an act that limits or restricts the performance of tasks by platform workers, which is carried out with the intention to further a work dispute with a platform operator.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: For instance, if a group of platform workers intentionally turn off their apps with the intent to compel a platform operator to agree to their terms of negotiation, we will consider them to be undertaking industrial action.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: In contrast, a platform worker will not be regarded as undertaking industrial action if he shares information on better terms offered by a competing platform operator and suggests that other platform workers switch operator to enjoy the better terms.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Because in the second scenario, there is no intent by the platform workers to further a work dispute with a platform operator.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Mr Tay also suggested allowing platform work associations to use digital voting for secret ballots since platform workers have no fixed workplaces.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We agree that platform workers may not have fixed workplaces or fixed schedules and hence a different way of conducting ballots may be needed.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Hence, we accepted the recommendations of the Tripartite Workgroup on Representation of Platform Workers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: To ensure the security and integrity of the voting process, we will implement strong safeguards including secure authentication systems.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Mr Ang Wei Neng sought clarification on whether platform work associations can negotiate with private hire car rental companies and taxi companies and represent permanent residents, or PRs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: The new legal framework allows platform work associations to represent platform workers and such platform workers can include PRs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Remember we said there is a two-pronged assessment of who is a platform operator – so, private hire car companies and taxi companies that do not fulfil the definition of platform operators and are therefore not platform operators, are not covered under the framework.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: But associations or societies can continue to engage such companies, which is already the case today.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Mr Ang also queried on the requirement that at least two-thirds of the officers in a platform work association must be active platform workers, and whether officers should be required to work a minimum number of hours each month to better stay connected and relevant to the platform workers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: In general, the representation framework for platform work sector is modelled after that of the trade unions, which has worked well and contributed to Singapore’s industrial harmony over the years.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: The two-thirds requirement is, for example, the same as that in the trade union space.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: On the point of having a fixed work hour eligibility criterion for officers, we have not set this requirement as we recognise that platform workers may not have a regular schedule every month.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Ms Jean See asked for the introduction of tripartite set-ups between sectoral platform work associations and platform operators.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Mr Pritam Singh, Ms See and Mr Louis Ng also suggested to require platform operators to make information on its algorithm and earnings transparent to platform workers, or to validate their algorithms against AI Verify for fairness and safety.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Ms See further suggested requiring platform operators to provide some form of income protection for platform workers if there is an outage in their app platform.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: These requirements are specified in clauses 13 and 14 of the Bill respectively.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Related to this, Mr Patrick Tay sought clarification on the different classes of platform workers mentioned in clause 13(4).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: To clarify, clause 13(4) will provide the Government with the flexibility to set different record retention periods for different groups of platform workers, for example, based on the type of platform services they provide.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Having said that, we currently have no plans to set different record retention periods.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: As mentioned earlier, algorithms may be proprietary, and regulating platform operators’ use of algorithms will impose significant compliance costs and affect the economic viability of platform operators.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Potential entrants may also be deterred from the market due to the fear of excessive regulatory burden.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Platform operators also need the flexibility to decide how to remunerate platform workers, in order to balance the demand and supply of services while keeping prices manageable for consumers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We should avoid being too heavy handed with regulation, which could stifle the innovation and sustainability of the platform economy, and lead to poorer outcomes for platform workers themselves.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Instead of the blunt tool of regulation, it is better to focus on the outcomes and empower stakeholders to negotiate for their interests.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This is why we are empowering platform work associations to negotiate with platform operators for better outcomes and to balance the relationship between platform workers and platform operators.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Platform work associations will be well placed to represent the interests of platform workers and negotiate a sustainable and mutually agreed solution at the individual platform operator level that takes into consideration all parties’ circumstances.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Platform work associations and platform operators are also free to establish and participate in tripartite platforms as needed, similar to how trade unions and employers interact today.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Beyond getting help from platform work associations, I would add that platform workers do have the choice to switch platforms, if they feel that they have been treated unfairly, or even when the app of one platform operator is facing technical issues.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This is how most people would operate today anyway – you arbitrage between the rates of different apps and switch from one to the other, and if one is not working, go to the next one.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: So, this is commonsense and people are already doing that today.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: I will move on to the concerns raised on the impact of this Bill on stakeholders.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Many Members have raised clarifications on the impact of this Bill on platform operators, platform workers and customers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Ms Yeo Wan Ling, Mr Yip Hon Weng, Mr Mark Lee, Mr Pritam Singh, Mr Ong Hua Han, Mr Leong Mun Wai, Ms Joan Pereira and Ms Mariam Jaafar have raised several concerns on whether the costs of these platform work protections will be passed to platform workers and customers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi spoke about assuaging the concerns of platform workers, platform operators and customers as we implement the Bill and Mr Neil Parekh requested Government assistance or incentives to help businesses make this transition.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: On the impact to workers, I have elaborated at length on the measures to prevent the passing of costs to workers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: So, I will not repeat the points here, except to add that ultimately, market competition is an important self-regulating force.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: It bears repeating that platform work associations will play an important role in representing the interests of platform workers and these workers will also have the choice to switch platforms if they feel that costs are unfairly passed over to them.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: On the impact to platform operators, the Government has been working closely with the companies who have stepped forward to seek advice on how to implement CPF and work injury compensation regimes for platform workers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We will continue to do so through existing structures.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This is the first time we are defining platform operators in legislation and we understand companies may have questions on whether they meet the definition of a platform operator.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: An example of a question, which Ms Usha Chandradas raised, is on the threshold of human intervention in the use of data that would define an entity as exercising management control over a worker.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: That said, I would like to highlight that whether an entity is exercising management control and the broader question of whether it is a platform operator is fact-dependent and companies should do their own due diligence checks to see if they fit the bill.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: MOM will provide support to companies to determine whether they are likely to be a platform operator, including through a self-assessment checklist.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Companies can also approach MOM if they still require further advice on their specific circumstances.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: As Ms Mariam Jaafar pointed out, as a society, all stakeholders should be prepared to do our part for platform workers to receive protections they need.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Platform operators will need to consider how best to manage the costs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Thus, it is a levelling up of what platform operators ought to have been paying, if they are to ensure basic protections for platform workers like what other employers have been doing for their employees all along.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Introducing CPF and work injury compensation for platform workers, therefore, ensures that platform operators who derive their sources of revenue from the hard work and risks taken by the platform workers, provide them with basic rights and protections.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: It will also ensure a level playing field for companies operating in Singapore to compete fairly in terms of business costs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: How do employers in non-platform sectors typically deal with these costs of providing protections for their employees?

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Well, it is part and parcel of running a business, so they build these costs into their overall operating cost and decide how to price their services based on a range of factors – costs, profitability and market competition.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: It would be disingenuous to reflect and charge these costs through a separate fee component.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Platform operators should think carefully before doing so, because, as I said, the market is a competitive one.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Such a move would be tantamount to passing the costs directly to customers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Customers have a choice to switch to other platforms where costs are shared more equitably or even stop using such platform services altogether and switch to other alternatives.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Platform work associations can work with platform operators to regularly publish these data, so workers and consumers can clearly see how the costs are shared across stakeholders to counter any claims of profiteering or loading of these costs onto the workers themselves.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Mr Yip Hon Weng, Ms Joan Pereira, Mr Ong Hua Han and Ms Usha Chandradas spoke about protecting platform workers from abuse and unfair reviews, with Mr Yip suggesting to provide mental health support for platform workers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: In this respect, the Protection from Harassment Act protects all individuals, including platform workers, from threatening, abusive or insulting words or behaviour.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Perpetrators may be prosecuted for offences under the Act.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: With these existing protections in place, we do not need to introduce additional protection for platform workers in this Bill.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Platform work associations can also work with platform operators on measures to deal with abusive customers, including blacklisting such customers and making available avenues of redress for platform workers who have been given unfair reviews.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Just like anyone else, platform workers who need mental health support can tap on the mental health services in community care settings, such as the Community Outreach Team, which offers basic emotional and psychological support.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Those facing job transitions can also seek no-cost assistance from Workforce Singapore's (WSG's) employment-focused peer support groups.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Platform work associations can also play an important role, as they are often the first port of call for platform workers when they are faced with challenges and I would encourage them to do more in this regard.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Mr Ong Hua Han also sought clarification on this Bill excluding other benefits, such as annual leave and medical benefits.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: For annual leave and medical benefits, we must recognise that these are relevant for employees where working hours and duties are fixed; whereas platform workers enjoy more flexibility compared to employees.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Platform workers and platform companies are keen to retain this flexibility, rather than be deemed as employees.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Thus, the Bill has focused on protections, such as CPF, work injury compensation and representation, which, we feel, will help platform workers be better protected, while maintaining the flexibility they desire.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Mr Ang Wei Neng asked for the number of platform workers who are non-Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Mr Gan Thiam Poh asked whether we will take action against foreigners illegally providing platform services.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Under the Employment of Foreign Manpower Act (EFMA), only foreigners with valid work passes are allowed to work in Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Foreign employees can only work in the occupation stated in their work passes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Foreign employees, who provide platform services, may face prosecution under the EFMA.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Ms Pereira spoke about the volatility and unpredictable nature of income earned in platform work.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: She and many other Members, such as Mr Liang Eng Hwa, Mr Ong Hua Han and Mr Mark Lee, also raised the need to support platform workers in upgrading their skills and transiting to other careers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This Bill is intended to protect those who have chosen to make platform work their occupation, especially those who face precarity because of their fluctuating incomes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: At the same time, as Members have pointed out, platform workers can also consider other forms of employment.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: There are measures in place to support platform workers who wish to transit to other sectors.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: For example, platform workers can tap on the Jobs and Skills Centres for career coaching service and advice.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: The scheme is targeted at employees who became unemployed due to involuntary reasons, such as retrenchment and dismissals, and platform workers are not included as they are not employees.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Ms Usha Chandradas asked whether legislative protection will be extended to freelancers, particular those in the arts community who can also be a vulnerable group.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: While this is outside the scope of this Bill, we take the points that the Member of Parliament has raised and will consider how this group may be better supported.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Platform workers face volatility and their incomes are subjected to the market forces of demand and supply.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This is a feature of the platform sector.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: And while we cannot change this, we can close the gaps in protections faced by platform workers and the sooner we do so, the better.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This could not have been done without strong tripartite dialogue and support.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Miss Rachel Ong and Mr Desmond Choo have aptly contrasted the acrimonious path that some overseas jurisdictions took in regulating platform work with our own tripartite approach.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: The tripartite system of close collaboration and dialogue between the Government, the Labour Movement, and businesses, has led us to a framework that balances the needs of all parties in a way sustainable for the platform ecosystem.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Platform operators, too, will benefit from a more engaged workforce and better industrial relations.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: This is not true and it is ridiculous for any governing party to not seek good relations with unions, when it is crucial for any government to work with unions and employers for the good of workers and the economy.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: An independent NTUC will be a stronger voice for workers as they will be better able to fight for workers' rights without fear or favour.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: I call for independent unions, not mindlessly confrontational unions.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: It is important for unions to work with the government of the day, but they should maintain their independence from the Government and should not be subordinated to it.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: This will benefit Singaporean workers and strengthen our country's institutions regardless of the political situation.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: It is about getting the best possible deal for Singaporean workers and for Singapore.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: And lastly, Senior Minister of State Koh mentioned ILO.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: ILO's Convention No 87 on freedom of association and protection of the right to organise, stresses that workers and employer organisations must be independent from public authorities, meaning the government, and free from government control or interference.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: This is found in Article 3(1), Article 3(2), Article 5, Article 8(2) and Article 11.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Instead of having a symbiotic relationship with the PAP, the NTUC should declare a symbiotic relationship with the people of Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: I believe yesterday, my colleague Mr Heng Chee How had addressed the point about independence and respect for the unions.
